title: Learned-projector QAOA for hierarchical optimization
authors: Kangyun Zhou, Dong An, Jin-Peng Liu
abstract: Many optimization problems reveal inexpensive structural information before requiring costly final evaluation, whereas the conventional quantum approximate optimization algorithm (QAOA) applies a single aggregate objective throughout. We introduce the learned-projector quantum alternating operator ansatz (LP-QAOA), a multistage protocol that freezes optimized circuits and uses their output states to define later projector mixers. We prove a stability theorem for LP-QAOA that bounds the propagation of approximation errors through successive frozen stages. Our analysis also shows how learned-projector mixing avoids the high-order tunnelling suppression of local mixers. We conduct state-vector simulations on block-constrained spin tiling (BCST) instances, where LP-QAOA achieves higher probabilities of sampling the optimum, lower estimated logical-resource requirements, and better trainability than the tested baselines. A supporting stochastic block model experiment extends LP-QAOA to optimization problems with soft hierarchical structure. Our results highlight the potential of LP-QAOA to improve variational quantum optimization by exploiting hierarchical problem structure.
summary: This paper introduces Learned-Projector QAOA (LP-QAOA), a novel multistage quantum algorithm designed to solve combinatorial optimization problems with hierarchical structure. It improves upon standard QAOA by freezing optimized intermediate states to define subsequent mixers, which enhances the ability to sample the true ground state. The results demonstrate that LP-QAOA is superior to existing methods on structured test cases.
main_problem: The paper addresses the challenge of improving variational quantum optimization for combinatorial problems that possess inherent hierarchical structure.
main_result: The proposed Learned-Projector QAOA (LP-QAOA) outperforms tested baselines by achieving higher probabilities of sampling the optimum and lower estimated resource requirements on structured instances.
method: LP-QAOA is a multistage protocol that recursively uses the optimized state from an earlier stage to define a projector mixer for subsequent stages, ensuring structural information is progressively incorporated.
model_or_system: The method is tested on Block-Constrained Spin Tiling (BCST) instances and Stochastic Block Model (SBM) graphs, which model constrained optimization problems. The core mechanism involves defining a mixer based on the projection onto a previously optimized quantum state.
key_observables: Probability of sampling the unique optimum ($P_{	ext{succ}}$), total estimated cost (Resource Units), and gradient magnitudes for training convergence.
important_parameters: The depth of the QAOA circuit (number of stages/layers) and the structure of the hierarchy (strict vs. soft).
main_assumptions: The stability theorem provides bounds on error propagation through successive frozen stages, assuming the learned structure provides a benefit over purely local interactions.
figures_summary: Figures summarize the LP-QAOA circuit structure, showing the uncomputation/re-preparation cycle for the mixer, and comparison tables (e.g., Table 13) compare LP-QAOA against block-XY and standard QAOA variants on success probability and cost.
paper_structure: The paper introduces LP-QAOA as a multistage protocol, proves a stability theorem for error bounding, and then validates its performance by comparing it against various QAOA baselines on structured optimization problems like BCST and SBM.
why_interesting: The concept of using learned projectors to guide quantum optimization by exploiting problem structure is highly relevant for developing scalable quantum algorithms beyond simple local Hamiltonians.
